about: 35-minute system design drills. Each step lists the key points a strong answer usually covers; after the drill you tick what you covered. Original prompts written for this app.

steps.label: Requirements
steps.ask: Functional must-haves, out of scope, and non-functional goals (latency, availability, consistency, scale).

steps.label: Estimates
steps.ask: Users, requests per second (read vs write), storage per year, bandwidth. Round numbers are fine.

steps.label: API
steps.ask: The main endpoints or events: inputs, outputs, status codes, idempotency, pagination.

steps.label: Data model
steps.ask: Entities, keys, which database and why, indexes, access patterns.

steps.label: Scaling
steps.ask: High-level boxes, caching, partitioning, replication, queues, the hot path, failure handling.

steps.label: Trade-offs
steps.ask: What you chose and gave up, bottlenecks, what you'd do next, how you'd monitor it.

prompts.title: URL shortener
prompts.brief: Design a service like bit.ly: turn long URLs into short links and redirect fast.
prompts.scale: 100 M new links / month, 10:1 reads to writes

requirements: Create short link, redirect, optional custom alias and expiry
Redirect latency is the key NFR (fast, highly available)
Analytics/out of scope stated explicitly
estimates: ~40 writes/s and ~400 reads/s average, peaks higher
Storage: ~500 bytes/link → tens of GB per year
Read-heavy: plan caching
api: GET /{code} → 301/302 redirect (and why you chose one)
Rate limiting / abuse protection on create
data: Key-value or wide-column store keyed by code
Code generation: base62 counter vs hash vs pre-generated key pool, collision handling
scaling: Cache hot codes (LRU, Redis) in front of the store
Partition by code; replicas for reads
Stateless app servers behind a load balancer

prompts.title: Rate limiter
prompts.brief: Design an API rate limiter that allows N requests per user per window across many servers.
prompts.scale: 1 M users, 50 k requests/s across 20 API servers

requirements: Limit per user / API key / IP, configurable rules
Low added latency, fails open or closed (decide)
Return 429 with retry-after
estimates: Counter state per active key fits in memory (MBs to a few GB)
Every request does one check: the limiter must be ~1 ms
data: Algorithm: token bucket vs sliding window log vs sliding window counter
Shared store (Redis) with atomic ops / Lua script
Key TTL equal to the window
scaling: Central store vs local counters synced periodically
Shard keys across Redis nodes
Handle the store being down (fail open + alert)

prompts.title: 1:1 and group chat
prompts.brief: Design a chat app like WhatsApp with 1:1 and small group messages, online status and delivery receipts.
prompts.scale: 50 M daily users, 2 B messages / day

requirements: Send/receive in real time, history, groups up to ~200
Delivered/read receipts, online presence
Messages must not be lost; ordering per conversation
estimates: ~25 k messages/s average, much higher peaks
Storage: ~100 bytes × 2 B/day → ~200 GB/day
Millions of concurrent connections
api: REST for history with cursor pagination
Client message id for idempotent retries
data: messages partitioned by conversation id, sorted by time/sequence
scaling: Connection gateway servers + a session registry (user → server)
Queue between gateway and storage; fan-out for groups
Offline users: store and push notification
tradeoffs: Fan-out on write for groups vs read

prompts.title: News feed
prompts.brief: Design a social news feed: users post, follow others, and see a ranked feed.
prompts.scale: 300 M users, average 200 follows, some celebrities with 50 M followers

requirements: Publish post, follow/unfollow, home feed with pagination
Feed loads fast; slight staleness is fine
Ranking (chronological first, then ranked)
estimates: Feed reads far exceed posts
Fan-out cost = posts × followers: celebrities dominate
Feed cache size per user (e.g. last 500 ids)
data: Precomputed feed lists in cache (user → post ids)
scaling: Fan-out on write for normal users
Fan-out on read (pull) for celebrities: hybrid
Async workers via queue; cache hydration
tradeoffs: Ranking signals and where they run

prompts.title: Notification service
prompts.brief: Design a service that sends push, SMS and email notifications for other teams' events.
prompts.scale: 10 M notifications / day, bursts of 1 M in minutes

requirements: Multiple channels, templates, user preferences / opt-out
At-least-once delivery without spamming duplicates
Scheduling and rate limits per user
estimates: Average ~120/s, bursts of thousands per second
Third-party provider limits are the bottleneck
data: notification log with status per channel
scaling: Queue per channel; worker pools; retries with backoff + dead-letter queue
Dedup by idempotency key
Priority lanes (OTP before marketing)

prompts.title: File storage and sync
prompts.brief: Design a Dropbox-like service: upload files, sync across devices, share links.
prompts.scale: 50 M users, 10 GB each on average

requirements: Upload/download, sync changes across devices, sharing
Large files resumable; no data loss
Version history
estimates: ~500 PB total storage: object storage, not a DB
Most files unchanged: dedupe saves a lot
api: Changes feed / long poll for sync
data: Metadata DB: files, versions, chunk lists, ownership
Chunks in object storage keyed by content hash
scaling: Split files into chunks, upload only changed chunks
Metadata sharded by user/namespace
CDN for downloads; notification service for sync
tradeoffs: Conflict handling (last write wins vs conflicted copy)
Strong consistency for metadata, eventual for chunks

prompts.title: Ride hailing (matching)
prompts.brief: Design the core of an Uber-like app: drivers send locations, riders request, the system matches them.
prompts.scale: 1 M active drivers sending a location every 4 s

requirements: Driver location updates, rider request, match, trip state
Matching latency in seconds; no driver double-booked
ETA and pricing out of scope or simplified
estimates: ~250 k location writes/s: keep in memory, not a DB per write
Only latest location matters for matching
api: Driver: location updates over a persistent connection
data: Geospatial index (geohash / quadtree / H3 cells) in memory
Trips table with a state machine
Location history to cheap storage asynchronously
scaling: Partition by city/region cell
Matching service queries nearby cells, offers to best driver
Lock/lease on a driver while offered
tradeoffs: Consistency of driver state vs speed

prompts.title: Search autocomplete
prompts.brief: Design type-ahead suggestions: as the user types, show the top 5 completions.
prompts.scale: 10 B queries / day, suggestions within 100 ms

requirements: Top-k suggestions per prefix, ranked by popularity
Very low latency; updates can lag (hourly/daily)
Filtering (offensive terms), personalisation optional
estimates: Several keystrokes per query → very high read QPS
Prefix index size: millions of prefixes × top-5
data: Trie with top-k cached at each node, or prefix → top-k table
Query logs aggregated offline into counts
scaling: Serve from memory; shard by prefix range
Rebuild index in batch, swap atomically
CDN/browser cache for popular prefixes
tradeoffs: Memory vs depth of precomputed top-k

prompts.title: Payment system
prompts.brief: Design a payment flow for a marketplace: charge buyers through a payment provider and pay sellers.
prompts.scale: 1 M payments / day, money must never be lost or double charged

requirements: Charge, refund, payouts; status visible to users
Correctness over speed: no double charge, auditable
Integrate with external PSPs
estimates: Low QPS (~12/s avg) but strict consistency
Ledger grows forever: plan archival
data: Payment state machine (created → authorised → captured → settled/failed)
scaling: Async processing with retries and idempotency
Reconciliation job against PSP reports
Outbox pattern for events
tradeoffs: Sync vs async confirmation to the user

prompts.title: Video streaming
prompts.brief: Design a YouTube-like service: upload videos and stream them smoothly on any network.
prompts.scale: 500 hours uploaded / minute, 1 B views / day

requirements: Upload, transcode, stream, basic metadata/search
Smooth playback (adaptive bitrate), global
Views counter can be approximate
estimates: Huge storage (multiple resolutions per video)
Bandwidth dominated by streaming: CDN essential
data: Raw + transcoded segments in object storage
scaling: Transcoding pipeline: queue + workers (DAG of tasks)
CDN with popular content pushed to edges
Adaptive bitrate in the client
tradeoffs: Pre-transcode all resolutions vs on demand for long tail

prompts.title: Web crawler
prompts.brief: Design a crawler that fetches a billion pages a month for a search index.
prompts.scale: 1 B pages / month, politeness per domain

requirements: Fetch, parse, extract links, store content
Politeness (robots.txt, per-host rate)
Avoid duplicates and traps
estimates: ~400 pages/s; ~100 KB/page → ~100 TB/month
DNS and network are the bottlenecks
api: Internal: seed URLs in, content + metadata out to the indexer
data: URL frontier with priority + per-host queues
Seen-URL set (Bloom filter) and content hashes for dedupe
scaling: Distributed workers partitioned by host hash
DNS cache; async I/O
Recrawl scheduling by change frequency

prompts.title: Ticket booking
prompts.brief: Design seat booking for movies or concerts where thousands rush for the same seats.
prompts.scale: Spikes of 100 k users for one popular show

requirements: Browse shows, pick seats, hold, pay, confirm
Never double-book a seat
Fairness under rush (queue/waiting room)
estimates: Normal load low, flash spikes huge
Seats per show small: contention, not volume, is the issue
data: Relational DB with row locks or optimistic concurrency
scaling: Virtual waiting room to meter traffic
Cache seat map, but book against the DB
Hold expiry job releases seats

prompts.title: Distributed cache
prompts.brief: Design a Redis/Memcached-like distributed cache used by many services.

requirements: get/set/delete with TTL, eviction
Sub-millisecond latency, high availability
Clients across many services
estimates: 2 TB / 64 GB per node → ~40 nodes plus replicas
Network round trip dominates latency
scaling: Add/remove nodes with minimal remapping
Primary–replica per shard, failover
Hot keys: replicate or local cache

prompts.title: Distributed job scheduler
prompts.brief: Design a scheduler that runs millions of delayed and recurring jobs reliably.
prompts.scale: 10 M jobs / day, many at the top of the hour

requirements: One-off and cron jobs, retries, status
At-least-once execution, no job lost
Visibility: history and failures
estimates: ~120 jobs/s average, big spikes on the hour
Job metadata small; execution time varies
scaling: Pollers claim due jobs with leases (SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) or time-bucketed queues
Workers pull from a queue
Jitter to spread top-of-hour spikes

prompts.title: Real-time leaderboard
prompts.brief: Design a live leaderboard for a game: update scores and show top 100 and a player's rank.

requirements: Update score, top-N, a player's rank and neighbours
Near real-time; ties handled
Daily/weekly boards
estimates: 10 M entries fit in memory
High write rate: in-memory structure
data: Durable score log in a DB
scaling: Shard by board; for huge boards, score-range buckets
Cache top-N
Rebuild from the log on failure

prompts.title: Metrics monitoring
prompts.brief: Design a monitoring system that collects metrics from thousands of servers, graphs them and alerts.
prompts.scale: 10 k hosts × 1 k metrics every 10 s

requirements: Ingest, store, query time series, alert on rules
Recent data fast; old data downsampled
Alerting must keep working during incidents
estimates: ~1 M data points/s
Compression matters (delta/gorilla encoding)
api: Query API with time range + aggregation
data: Time-series DB: series id + timestamp + value
scaling: Ingestion via queue (Kafka) to writers
Shard by series id
Alert evaluator separate from query path
